notes:
K8Secret 0.6.11 — clusters that authenticate with a client certificate.

If K8Secret failed on one Mac with 'a TLS error caused the secure connection to fail' while kubectl worked fine on the same machine and the same kubeconfig, this release is the fix, and the cause was not your cluster.

TLS 1.2 asks for your client certificate during the handshake. TLS 1.3 moved that request to after the handshake, and several managed API server front ends — Azure's among them — ask for nothing during it. macOS does not do the post-handshake version, so K8Secret was never asked for the certificate it was holding, never sent it, and the server closed a connection it considered anonymous. Whether TLS 1.3 gets used at all is decided by the operating system, which is why the same configuration worked on one Mac and not the next, and why kubectl was never affected.

Clusters that use a client certificate now negotiate TLS 1.2, where the request arrives in time to answer it. Clusters that use a token or a credential plugin are unchanged. Both still require a modern cipher with forward secrecy.
